Q2. Which of the following equations is correct?
A. 1 min = 1 s.
This incorrectly treats a minute as equal to a second.
B. 1 = 60.
This drops units entirely and asserts a false numerical equality.
C. 1 min = 60 s.
A minute is defined as sixty seconds, so the unit conversion is correct.
D. 60 min = 1 s.
This inverts the conversion and mixes incompatible magnitudes.

Q3. Which option has the incorrect unit?
A. Momentum: kg · m/s.
Momentum correctly has units of mass times velocity (kg · m/s).
B. Power: J/s.
Power is energy per time, so J/s (watt) is correct.
C. Pressure: N/m3.
Pressure is force per area (N/m2), so N/m3 has the wrong dimension.
D. Force: kg · m/s2.
Force has units kg · m/s2 (newton), which matches this expression.

Q7. A soccer ball is kicked from the ground with speed u0 at an angle ϕ above
the horizontal (ignore air resistance). What is the speed of the ball when it is
at maximum height?
A. u0.
The speed is not generally unchanged because the vertical component decreases to zero.
B. u0 cos ϕ.
At the top the vertical velocity is zero, so the speed equals the constant horizontal component
u0 cos ϕ.
C. u0 sin ϕ.
This is the initial vertical component, which becomes zero at maximum height.
D. 0.
Only the vertical component becomes zero at the top; the horizontal component remains
nonzero.

the x axis from x = −1.2 m to x = 3.6 m. What is the work, in joules, done by
the force on the particle?
A. −28.8 J.
This incorrectly uses the y-component (or both components) even though the displacement has
no y-component.
B. 12.0 J.
The displacement is ∆⃗r = (4.8 m)ˆı, so W = F⃗ · ∆⃗r = (2.50)(4.8) = 12.0 J.
C. 0 J.
Work is not zero because there is a nonzero force component along the displacement direction
(x).
D. 30.0 J.
This likely comes from using the force magnitude instead of the x-component in the dot product.

Q12. A 3.0 kg cart initially moving at 4.0 m/s collides with a wall and rebounds
at a speed of 2.0 m/s moving backward. The collision lasts for 0.10 seconds.
What is the average force exerted on the cart during the collision?
A. 60 N.
This underestimates the force by not using the full change in velocity (including the reversal in
direction).
B. 120 N.
This typically comes from subtracting speeds without accounting correctly for the sign change
or the time interval.
C. 180 N.
Taking forward as positive, ∆v = (−2.0 − 4.0) = −6.0 m/s so Favg = m∆v/∆t =
3.0(−6.0)/0.10 = −180 N (magnitude 180 N).
D. None of the above is correct.
Option C matches the impulse-momentum calculation, so “none” cannot be correct.
